Deep indigo spreads like velvet, the first star trembling awake.
Twilight deepens slowly, indigo pooling between the carnival spires.
One star appears, needle-bright, stitched into the darkening blue.
Molten gold bleeds at the horizon, the sunset quietly dissolving.
Rose swallows the gold, the sky blushing itself toward night.
The last ember of sunset floats above the glowing fairground.
A harvest moon rises vast and amber, draped in silver mist.
Mist halos the low moon, soft as breath on cold glass.
The great moon hangs enormous, honeyed, close enough to touch.
Aurora ribbons drift green and violet, slow as dreaming silk.
Soft green light breathes across the sky in wavering curtains.
Violet and jade aurora threads unravel gently above the tents.
The Milky Way arcs overhead, a river of dissolved pearls.
A broad band of starlight rivers across the whole dark sky.
Ten thousand stars crowd together, streaming their quiet silver road.
Below the hills, warm amber clouds glow like sunken lanterns.
A luminous cloud-sea burns amber, softly lit from somewhere beneath.
Sky-lanterns drift upward, paper moons rising to join the stars.
Dozens of lanterns climb slowly, warm gold among the cold stars.
A lantern floats past Venus, its flame a soft amber whisper.
Falling stars streak and vanish, silver threads pulled through dark cloth.
A meteor dissolves in silence, leaving only a memory of light.
One violet dusk, one bright wishing-star, one held breath.
The full moon lies mirrored in the lake, perfectly still, complete.
Pale pink dawn touches the water, and the night quietly folds.
